findings.problem: The launch plan's in-memory kernels are not the live spec authority. build_launch_plan copies approved argv/env/metadata into plan['kernels'], but run_jupyter never writes those specs and LocalKernelSpecManager.get_kernel_spec always loads JSON from directories['data']/kernels, then compares. kernel_dirs is forced to that private path (so env/share Jupyter kernels are invisible) and ensure_native_kernel is False.
findings.concrete_failure: On a clean service runtime tree the server can pass initialize and the security contract, then python3/ir lookup raises NoSuchKernel (or the Lab kernel list is empty). Instructional Python/R therefore cannot run from this startup path even when local_kernel_specs is valid. Disk also becomes a second authority: a matching file is required, a drifted file is silently unusable.
findings.repair: Make plan['kernels'] the only spec source. Override find_kernel_specs/get_all_specs/get_kernel_spec to return jupyter_client KernelSpec objects built from the approved dict (argv, display_name, language, env={}, metadata local-provisioner) without requiring kernel.json. If files are still written for Jupyter compatibility, run_jupyter must mkdir the private kernels dir and write those JSON files from the plan before initialize, then keep the exact-match guard.
findings.acceptance_test: Build a plan with local_kernel_specs python3 and ir; leave <runtime_dir>/data/kernels absent. After constructing LocalKernelSpecManager (or starting IsolatedServerApp), get_kernel_spec('python3') and get_kernel_spec('ir') return argv/env/metadata identical to plan['kernels']; get_kernel_spec('python') and any extra name raise NoSuchKernel; find_kernel_specs() is exactly those two names. Repeat after placing a drifted python3/kernel.json with a different argv — still the plan argv wins, or the kernel is refused, never the drifted argv.

findings.problem: Private process paths are only string assignments. directories lists config/data/runtime/profile/temp/ipython/lab-settings/lab-workspaces/r-libraries, and environment sets TEMP/TMP plus USERPROFILE/HOME/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA under profile, but neither build_launch_plan nor run_jupyter creates those directories. validate_process_environment only checks TEMP/TMP are non-empty strings, not existing dirs. Python tempfile skips a TEMP value that is not an existing directory and falls back (often cwd).
findings.concrete_failure: First start with only runtime_dir present: base/temp does not exist, tempfile.gettempdir() is not the private temp, and Jupyter/ipykernel scratch files can land in cwd, commonly runtime root_dir (notebook MAIN/user content) — the same overlap the planner forbids between notebook files and service state. Missing temp can also break kernel start without a NotebookServiceError.
findings.repair: Before os.environ.clear(), create every plan['directories'] entry plus profile/AppData/Roaming and profile/AppData/Local (and the empty-r-startup file the R_* variables name). Re-run private_path_check on the new tree. Fail with a NotebookServiceError if TEMP/TMP is not a directory. Do not start Jupyter until tempfile.gettempdir() equals that private temp.
findings.acceptance_test: Fresh runtime_dir with no subfolders; build_launch_plan then the materialize/start path. Assert each directories value is a dir; Path(environment['TEMP']).is_dir(); after env apply, tempfile.gettempdir() equals that path and is not runtime['root_dir']; creating a NamedTemporaryFile does not add files under root_dir.

limits: Reviewed only the supplied notebook_service.py functions. Unseen helpers (_runtime_validator, _local_path, _inside, verify_private_path, read_password_hash, current_windows_account) were treated as working, not as proven safe.
Did not re-open the prior N1–N4 dispositions (process-floor checks, NoSuchKernel vs abort, env={}, trust_xheaders False).
No live Jupyter, HTTPS/WSS proxy, service logon, startup task, reboot, iPad, or kernel-execution proof was claimed or required.
UI/register/companion-notebook conversion and route wiring were not in this packet and were not inferred as passing or failing.
root_dir remains a trusted single-user workspace, not an OS sandbox. Hypothetical TOCTOU on a cooperating filesystem was not counted.
Did not require per-kernel env, R_HOME inheritance, or a multitenant redesign.
